new_statements.relation_note: Survey-wide note: stress is non-phonemic in all languages of the comparative wordlist and is written only when it does NOT fall on the first syllable lacking schwa; none of the 45 Aru forms carries a stress mark (e.g. yitən, uwalan, sərptən, səneimpən, pəriŋ, nəmalal, yəlawan, nantiyou), so every recorded Aru word is stressed on its first non-schwa syllable.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is not phonemic; by Laycock's convention the default (unmarked) stress falls on the first syllable of the word whose vowel is not schwa (schwa syllables are skipped), and all recorded Aru forms are unmarked, i.e. initial stress unless the first vowel is ə, then the next full-vowel syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: Forms whose stress falls elsewhere would carry an acute accent; none of the 45 Aru items does. Words consisting only of schwa syllables (e.g. sərptən) are not addressed by the convention.
